A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamText in High Fidelity Scene Text Synthesis. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and editing results, loss and hyperparameter ablations, attention analyses, and appendix experiments on balanced supervision.

after.justification: v2 retains original DreamText experiments, revises the loss-ablation results, and adds quantitative and qualitative comparisons with AnyText.

M1.justification: Character-mask construction, the four losses, joint text-encoder/U-Net training, alternating optimization and balanced supervision remain unchanged. The approximately 25,000-step warm-up newly mentioned in the method prose was already specified in v1 Figure 4.

E1.justification: Both versions use SynthText, LAION-OCR, ICDAR13 and TextSeg for the same scene-text reconstruction and editing tasks. Additional AnyText examples remain within the existing scene-text setting; no new dataset or distinct test scenario is established.

E2.justification: AnyText is added to Table 1 and the existing qualitative comparisons, alongside a dedicated comparison in v2 Figure 10. MOSTEL, SD-Inpainting, DiffSTE, TextDiffuser and UDiffText are retained.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds LPIPS to the loss-ablation evaluation. The editing description also drops v1's explicit equal-length replacement requirement, leaving replacement lengths unspecified; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Reported data counts, training budgets and main evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The retained cumulative-loss ablation gains LPIPS evidence about the losses' effects on perceptual similarity, alongside revised scores. The loss combinations, hyperparameter sweep, balanced-supervision comparison and attention-evolution analyses are retained; Tables 3 and 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice and attention mIoU plots remain unchanged, including in the appendices.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially replaces the numerical evidence about loss contributions: Base reconstruction/editing/FID changes from 0.362/0.217/51.29 to 0.218/0.060/26.78, and full-loss FID changes from 15.79 to 12.13. Intermediate scores also change and LPIPS entries are added; these are revised reports, not established same-setting gains. Table 1 adds AnyText, including FID 22.73 and LPIPS 0.0651, while all pre-existing Table 1 scores and Tables 3–4 remain unchanged. New qualitative comparisons and an 8.5-second inference-time result also appear.

T1.justification: The attention and mask definitions, thresholding formula, loss equations and optimization reasoning are retained. Equation numbering changes, but no mathematical definition, derivation, assumption or proof is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about character fidelity, joint representation learning, heuristic alternating optimization, balanced supervision and superiority over existing methods.

C2.justification: The results discussion replaces TextDiffuser with AnyText when discussing strong image quality but weaker text accuracy relative to DreamText, extending the restricted-representation and deflected-attention explanation to AnyText. Other mechanism explanations and the multi-region and privacy limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies Stable Diffusion v2.0 inpainting as the ablation base, reports 8.5-second inference time, and states that AnyText follows its original paper's settings. The direct repository link is replaced with a project-page link. Existing hardware, training schedules, batch size, learning rate and loss weights are retained.

R1.justification: AnyText by Tuo et al. is added as cited and evaluated prior work. The related-work discussion and broader research positioning remain largely unchanged; publication and citation-format updates to existing references do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order are retained, with limited clarifications, changed author and affiliation text, unnumbered headings and author-year citations. v2 introduces two blank section references in Method and leaves a stale 'Eq. 1' reference where the intended diffusion objective is now unnumbered.

P2.justification: The conversion from one-column to two-column formatting substantially resizes and relocates figures and tables. Comparison grids gain AnyText columns, Figure 5 gains an input-prompt annotation, Table 2 gains an LPIPS column, and a new Figure 10 is added. v1 appendix Figures 10–12 are retained as v2 Figures 11–13.

improvement.justification: AnyText comparisons, LPIPS ablation results and explicit identification of the ablation base modestly strengthen the experimental reporting. The full-loss FID in Table 2 now also matches Table 1 at 12.13, versus 15.79 previously. These gains are partly offset by unexplained ablation-score revisions, newly broken cross-references and less explicit editing-length requirements, limiting the overall improvement.
